Print Book Sales Rose Slightly in 2025

# Print Book Sales Rose Slightly in 2025

By Jim Milliot |

Jan 09, 2026

For the second consecutive year, unit sales of print books were up at outlets that report to Circana BookScan, hitting 762.4 million in 2025 for the year ended Dec. 27, 2025. That marks a 0.3% increase over 2024, which in turn saw sales grow 0.5% over 2023. Since sales peaked in 2021 at 839.7 million copies, they have settled at levels higher than before the pandemic, though not as high as many publishers had hoped.

Postpandemic, adult fiction—helped by the emergence of BookTok—has been the strongest segment, and adult fiction sales did increase again in 2025, but they were up just 1%, compared to a nearly 5% increase in 2024 over 2023. Sales in the romance category rose 3.9%, to almost 44 million units, while fantasy sales fell 8.7%, to 24.1 million. BookScan doesn’t have a romantasy category, but the big driver in romance was the romantasy favorite Onyx Storm (Wing and Claw Collection) by Rebecca Yarros, which sold nearly 1.7 million copies during the year. The standard edition of Onyx Storm sold another 573,000 copies.

Elsewhere in adult fiction, after two years of declines, sales of graphic novels bounced back, rising 9.2% in 2025, to 25.9 million units. Science fiction posted the largest increase among adult fiction categories, with sales up 22.1%, to just over six million units. Suspense and thriller sales fell 2.2%, to 25.5 million units.

Adult nonfiction remains the industry’s largest segment by a wide margin, even with unit sales down 1.5% in 2025, following a 0.5% drop in 2024. Among the segment’s largest categories, religion posted a 5.4% increase, with unit sales approaching 67 million. Self-help had a good year, with sales up 14.7%, led by The Let Them Theory by Mel Robbins, which sold more than 2.8 million copies in 2025, making it the bestselling book of the year at BookScan outlets. On the downside, sales of biographies, autobiographies, and memoirs dropped 7%, while sales of business and economic books fell 3.9%.

The children’s fiction category had a mild rebound last year, with unit sales up 1.6%. The top titles were from two perennial bestselling authors: Jeff Kinney’s latest Wimpy Kid installment, Partypooper, sold more than 817,000 copies, while Dav Pilkey’s latest Dog Man entry, Big Jim Believes, sold more than 767,000 copies. Children’s nonfiction posted a 3.6% sales increase. Two bibles topped the category bestseller list: The Action Bible: God’s Redemptive Story by Sergio Cariello sold nearly 478,000 copies, and The Beginner’s Bible: Timeless Children’s Stories sold more than 331,000 copies.

The young adult segment had mixed results, with the larger fiction category posting a 1.8% decline, while nonfiction sales increased 3.8%. The decline in fiction came despite a big showing by Suzanne Collins’s Sunrise on the Reaping, which sold just over two million copies.

As usual, the vast majority of titles topping the 2025 bestseller list came from large publishers. The bestselling book from an independent publisher was Lights Out by Navessa Allen, which was published by Zando and sold more than 595,000 copies.

# Who sold the most books in 2025?

by

| Apr 23, 2026 | Articles, For Readers

## Who sold the most books in 2025?

I have been looking back at who sold the most books each year since 2022 here at Horror Tree. Every year, this question is not as easy to answer as it seems as each site has different information and metrics, but often, the same names and books pop up on most of the lists. I work to balance variety with accuracy when I choose the authors to feature, that is why once again, this list will be ten of the best-selling authors in 2025 (in no particular order) based on a variety of sources listed at the end of the article. If you are interested in who was on top the last three years, you can find them here: 2022, 2023, 2024.

To the surprise of no one, the Top Five Publishers dominate the best-seller lists each year, with Penguin Random House at the top with 38% of hardcover bestsellers in 2025. Indie and small presses make up a much smaller share of the market, but hardcover sales for the Top Five slipped down to 83% of the market from 86% in 2024, showing a modest growth for independent publishers. As well, the Independent Publisher Caucus, a collective of 117 small and independent publishers, launched the Independent Press Top 40 bestseller list in tandem with the American Booksellers Association this year with weekly bestseller lists of books from indie presses being sold at indie bookstores across the USA. I am excited about this because it will make it easier for me to include more indie best-sellers on this list next year.

## #1 – Suzanne Collins

Top-Selling Books: Sunrise on the Reaping, The Hunger Games

Suzanne Collins is one of the most famous authors of children’s and young adult fiction. She is best known for her dystopian YA series, The Hunger Games, and her children’s fantasy series, The Underland Chronicles. Collins began her career in 1991 as a writer for children’s television shows. She made the transition to books when she came up with the idea for The Underland Chronicles and wrote five books between 2003 and 2007. Then, in 2008, she published the first book in The Hunger Games trilogy, followed by a prequel in 2020.

2025 saw the release of a second Hunger Games prequel, Sunrise on the Reaping (SotR), which focuses on the backstory of Katniss’ mentor, Haymitch Abernathy and his time in the games. SotR catapulted to the top of the children and YA bestseller list, selling over 2 million hardcovers (including the one on my own shelf). As well, a feature film based on the book is coming to theatres this November. The success of SotR also boosted Collins’ other works, with The Hunger Games reappearing on top selling lists.

## #2 – Freida McFadden

Top-Selling Books: The Housemaid, The Housemaid’s Secret, The Tenant, The Crash

For the third year in a row now, Freida McFadden has found her way onto this list with her psychological thrillers. McFadden is the pseudonym of Sarah Cohen. Cohen’s first career was as a physician. She studied mathematics at Harvard University and later attended medical school. Throughout her career in medicine, she was writing fiction and submitting manuscripts. She self-published her first book in 2013, and since then, she has published 30 novels, including The Housemaid, which was adapted into a film in 2025 starring Amanda Seyfried and Sydney Sweeney. Beyond this, she had eight books that held double-digit stays on the bestseller list in 2025.

## #3 – Rebecca Yarros

Top-Selling Books: Fourth Wing, Iron Flame, Onyx Storm

None of my best-selling lists would be complete without at least one Romantasy bestseller. This year, it is Rebecca Yarros who dominated the book lists. Her best-known series is the Empyrean series. The first book, Fourth Wing was released in April 2023, followed by Iron Flame in November. The third book in the series, Onyx Storm, came out in January 2025 and sold more than 2.7 million copies within the first week. As well, in January, she held the top 3 spots on the New York Times’ hardcover bestseller list.

Yarros began writing while her husband was deployed in Afghanistan. Fourth Wing is her 20th novel. Along with her sons, Yarros has Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, which is a genetic connective tissue disorder. She cites her illness as one of her inspirations, as she had never read a fantasy novel that had a protagonist with physical limitations like hers, so she chose to write one.

## #4 – Mel Robbins

Top-selling book: The Let Them Theory

Each year, I like to include at least one top-selling non-fiction book, and this year, Mel Robbins’ book, The Let Them Theory (TLTT) was an easy choice since it was the #1 best selling book on Amazon in 2025. Originally published in 2024, TLTT climbed the list in 2025 in part because Robbins went on her first global speaking tour, which began on May 2, 2025 and visited 31 cities across North America. The book is a self-help book that focuses on letting go of other people’s judgments and opinions. Robbins also hosts a podcast and has written two other self-help books.

## #5 – Louise Penny

Top-selling book: The Black Wolf

Louise Penny is a Canadian author of crime fiction. Her most famous series stars Chief Inspector Armand Gamache and is set in Quebec. She has sold millions of copies worldwide and has repeatedly been featured in the number 1 spot on the New York Times Best Seller List. Her latest book in the series, The Black Wolf, in which Gamache has to stop a deadly terrorist ring, reached the number one spot in November 2025. As well, The Black Wolf was the bestselling book by a Canadian author in Canada for 2025.

## #6 – Percival Everett

Top-selling book: James

Percival Everett is an American Pulitzer Prize-winning author and a professor of English who has written over 20 novels as well as numerous short stories and poetry. In 2024, he published James, a reimagining of the Adventures of Huckleberry Finn by Mark Twain, told from the point of view of the slave, Jim, who travels with him. James won both a National Book Award and the Pulitzer Prize. In 2025, Everett was the bestselling Black author in 2025, according to a new list compiled by the African American Literature Book Club, beating out Kamala Harris and Octavia E. Butler.

## #7 – Dan Brown

Top-selling book: The Secret of Secrets

Dan Brown wrote a few books before hitting the best seller list with his breakout hit, The Da Vinci Code in 2003. Due to its success, his previous books, which had seen little success, reached the bestseller list in 2004. The protagonist of his series is Robert Langdon, a Harvard University professor who goes on thrilling treasure hunts, reminiscent of Indiana Jones. The Secret of Secrets is the sixth book in this series and was at the number one spot on the New York Times Bestseller List for two weeks in a row in 2025.

## #8 – Jeff Kinney

Top-selling book: Partypooper (Diary of a Wimpy Kid #20)

Of the top twenty bestselling books of 2025, according to Publishers Weekly, seven are children’s books, the top of which belongs to Jeff Kinney, author of the Diary of a Wimpy Kid series. The series is an illustrated children’s novel series and media franchise that follows a middle-schooler named Greg Heffley who illustrates his life in the eponymous diary. Kinney first came up with the characters in 1998, but spent eight years conceiving the first book before showing it to a publisher. The series began as a website with daily entries before Kinney signed a multi-book deal in 2006 to launch the book series. It has been a remarkable hit, and this is the third time I have included him on this list.

## #9 – Dav Pilkey

Top-selling books: Big Jim Begins (Dog Man #13), Big Jim Believes (Dog Man #14)

With two of the seven spots on the top 20 list, Dav Pilkey certainly deserves to be included on this list for the third time, as well. Pilkey’s Dog Man series is about a crime-fighting dog who likes to dress up as “The Bark Knight”. The series is a spin-off of Pilkey’s other famous series, Captain Underpants. The titular Big Jim is a cat who is a friend of Dog Man, and has his own superhero identity, “Commander Cupcake”. Pilkey wrote his first book in 1987, World War Won, and published Captain Underpants in 1997.

## #10 – Navessa Allen

## Top-selling book: Lights Out

My last entry, Lights Out by Navessa Allen, is very different from the last two books. Described as a “fast-paced dark romance with a morally gray male lead,” this book comes with a long list of trigger warnings. I am including it because it is the bestselling book from an independent publisher (Zando), having sold more than 595,000 copies and sitting at number eleven on Publisher Weekly’s top 20 list. Allen has had a variety of jobs, bartending, serving in the military, building flight simulators, farming, etc. She worked these jobs while pursuing her career as a full-time writer.

Melody lives in Ontario, Canada and writes short, speculative fiction that has been published by several small presses. She is also an avid reviewer who writes reviews and articles for The Horror Tree and on her blog, Melody Writes. Melody is a member of Sisters in Crime and is the secretary for the Ontario chapter of the Horror Writers Association. She earned her Master of Arts studying Ancient Greek and Roman Studies and often infuses her work with elements of Greek mythology.

Publishers Weekly list of bestselling novels in the United States

This is a list of lists of bestselling novels in the United States as determined by Publishers Weekly. The list features the most popular novels of each year from 1895 through 2020.

The standards set for inclusion in the lists – which, for example, led to the exclusion of the novels in the Harry Potter series from the lists for the 1990s and 2000s– are currently unknown.

For many years, the list was maintained by Alice Payne Hackett, who also published a decennial series which summarized and commented on the best sellers of the previous decade. Her Seventy Years of Bestsellers 1895–1965 was published in 1970.

## 1890s

This is a list of bestselling novels in the United States from 1895 through 1899, as determined by The Bookman, a New York–based literary journal. Without the international copyright law which came into force in 1891, these volumes could have been printed and published by anyone, the change in this state of affairs made it possible to compile accurate sales figures.

Notable attempts to compile a list of best-selling books in the United States prior to 1895 include The Popular Book: A History of America's Literary Taste (1950) by James D. Hart.

# Women Ruled the 2023 Bestseller List

By Jim Milliot |

Women authors fared very well at the top of the PW overall bestseller list in 2023. Colleen Hoover, who reigned supreme in 2022, also had a stellar 2023, with her It Ends with Us edging out It Starts with Us for the top-selling title in the year by about 48,000 print copies. A third Hoover novel, Verity, sold more than 935,000 copies. The three books sold a combined total of about 3.4 million copies at outlets that report to Circana BookScan.

The two biggest surprise hits in the year were Rebecca Yarros’s Fourth Wing and Iron Flame, which sold about 1.2 million and one million copies, respectively. A third woman author who had a big 2023 bestseller was Bonnie Garmus, whose 2022 Lessons in Chemistry sold just over one million copies thanks in part to the Apple TV+ series of the same name. Overall, 17 of the top 25 bestselling print books in 2023 were written by women.

Two memoirs sold particularly well last year, with Spare by Prince Harry selling more than 1.2 million copies, good enough for third place on the 2023 list, and The Woman in Me by Britney Spears in 10th place, selling more than 908,000 copies. Barbra Streisand’s My Name Is Barbra, priced at $47, has sold more than 212,000 copies since its release on November 7.

In a year where adult sales did noticeably better than sales of children’s books, only six children’s titles cracked the top 25 bestseller list chart, led by Dav Pilkey’s Dog Man: Twenty Thousand Fleas Under the Sea, which was also the only children’s book to sell more than one million copies at BookScan outlets.

Print Book Sales Saw a Small Sales Increase in 2024

# Print Book Sales Saw a Small Sales Increase in 2024

### After two years of declines, print sales inched up in 2024

by Jim Milliot |

Jan 10, 2025

Though unit sales of print books rose by less than 1% in 2024 over 2023, it was the first annual increase in three years at outlets that report to Circana BookScan. Unit sales totaled 782.7 million in the year ended Dec. 28, 2024, compared to 778.3 million in 2023. While 2024 sales were down from the 839.7 million units sold in the peak year of 2021, the figure was higher than the 759.6 million print copies sold in 2020, the first year of the pandemic.

In 2024, sales gradually improved over the course of the year and saw a 1.6% increase in the fourth quarter. For the full year, the sales performance followed a familiar path, as adult fiction was once again the driver, with units rising 4.8%. Fantasy had the biggest increase in the adult segment, up 35.8%. Sarah J. Maas and Rebecca Yarros were the queens of romantasy in the year, with each landing two books among the year’s top sellers. Maas’s A Court of Thorns and Roses and A Court of Mist and Fury moved about 1.3 million and 791,000 copies, respectively, while sales of Yarros’s Iron Flame and Fourth Wing sold nearly 1.7 million copies combined last year.

On the romance side of the romantasy equation, Colleen Hoover’s It Ends with Us and It Starts with Us sold a total of more than 1.6 million copies. The bestselling book of the year was The Women by Kristin Hannah, which sold nearly 1.5 million copies. Overall, sales of romance books rose almost 9% in 2024. Graphic novels had a second consecutive year of declines, with sales falling 11.5%. Even so, with 24.4 million copies sold, graphic novels was the fifth largest of adult fiction’s 12 subcategories.

Sales in the biggest category, adult nonfiction, fell 0.5% in the year. Of the five titles to sell more than one million copies last year, only one was nonfiction: The Eras Tour Book, self-published by Taylor Swift, sold more than 1.2 million copies. (It was ineligible to be included on bestseller lists due to its being sold exclusively through Target.) James Clear’s Atomic Habits finished another year as the category’s most popular book, selling 982,000 copies. Nonfiction also had the year’s biggest surprise bestseller when J.D. Vance’s backlist book, Hillbilly Elegy, jumped on the bestseller list after he was named Donald Trump’s running mate, going on to sell more than 700,000 copies.

Among the adult nonfiction subcategories, religion books had the biggest increase, with sales up 11.5%, selling more than 64 million units.

The top children’s book in 2024 was Dav Pilkey’s The Scarlet Shedder, the 12th volume in Pilkey’s Dog Man series, which sold nearly 1.3 million copies. Another popular series, Jeff Kinney’s Wimpy Kid, produced a hit with Hot Mess, which sold more than 748,000 copies. Despite the two powerhouses, total juvenile fiction sales slipped 1.3% overall.

The top-selling young adult fiction title last year was If He Had Been with Me, which sold more than 711,000 copies. YA fiction sales have softened each year after peaking in 2021, when 31.2 million copies were sold. Last year, sales in the category were just under 30.2 million copies, down 4.3% from 2023.

Colleen Hoover Was Queen of 2022's Bestseller List

# Colleen Hoover Was Queen of 2022's Bestseller List

By Jim Milliot |

Jan 06, 2023

It is something of an understatement to say that Colleen Hoover, a 2022 PW Notable, dominated last year’s overall bestsellers list. Hoover had the top three books of the year, and her novels sold 14.3 million print copies at outlets that report to NPD BookScan. Of the 25 books on the list, eight were Hoover titles, and two, It Ends with Us and Verity, sold more than two million copies each.

Last year was a very good year for adult fiction overall, as evidenced by the 8.5% annual sales increase posted by the category (see “The Winning Streak Ends,” p. 8) and by its prevalence at the top of the overall bestsellers list. Fifteen of the 25 top-selling books were adult fiction, and another five titles were either juvenile fiction or young adult fiction. The top-selling nonfiction book was James Clear’s Atomic Habits, at #6.

The only other author besides Hoover to place more than one title on the top 25 list was Emily Henry, who scored with Book Lovers and People We Meet on Vacation, at #21 and #25, respectively. The strong showing by Hoover also crowded out some perennial chart toppers, including James Patterson, whose Run, Rose, Run (written with Dolly Parton) was at #26 (with about 515,000 copies sold), and John Grisham, whose The Boys from Biloxi sold about 495,000 copies, landing it at #29 on the overall list.

The list clearly shows that readers were ready for some escapism in 2022, after nearly three years of pandemic concerns and an ever more divisive political environment. The bestselling title related to politics last year was Red Handed: How American Elites Get Rich by Helping China Win by Peter Schweizer, which sold about 245,000 copies. The top-performing book critical of former president Trump was Maggie Haberman’s Confidence Man, which sold about 127,000 copies; former vice president Mike Pence’s memoir sold approximately 112,000 copies.
